stories.title: Spirit of 1676: remembering the Native American cataclysm of King Philip’s war
stories.summary: The conflict that tore through New England 350 years ago was the bloodiest per capita in colonial or US history Massachusetts is proud of its ties to the American Revolution. From Paul Revere’s Ride to the siege of Boston, the past year-plus has been devoted to celebrating 250 years of US independence. Yet during this time, the state, and New England in general, has given far less attention to an older, more complex remembrance: The 350th anniversary of King Philip’s war. King Philip, or Metacom, was an Indigenous leader from the Pokanoket people. Alarmed by English colonists’ infringement of Indigenous rights, from seizing land to proselytizing, Metacom led an alliance of New England tribes – including the Pokanoket, Nipmuc and Narragansett – in an existential struggle for control of the region. A win is a win in this league, but I can't write that all wins are viewed as equal. Over time, essentially all clubs regress to the mean in those tight contests. She spent nearly 20 years believing she had MS. Then her diagnosis changed.
stories.summary: DeMonica Amerson was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis at 21. Nearly two decades later, she received devastating news. DeMonica Amerson's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in 2001 had been a shock. No one in her family had ever had the autoimmune condition, and it had been difficult to diagnose. Doctors had first thought she had optic neuritis because her symptoms were in her eyes. Then they suspected lupus. After a spinal tap, she was diagnosed with MS. At the time, Amerson had never heard about the condition. She had just graduated from college and expected to be in the prime of her life. Instead, she had to give herself daily shots to treat the condition.
